gamma_events.title: Highest temperature in Munich on August 19?
gamma_events.description:
This market will resolve based on the highest temperature recorded in the 'Daily Observations' table on Weather Underground, not the figure displayed in the 'Day High & Low' summary section; in the event of any discrepancy between the two, the Daily Observations table shall be the primary resolution source not the Day High & Low section.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded at the Munich Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 19 Aug '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from Wunderground, specifically the highest temperature recorded for all times on this day for the Munich Airport Station, available here: https://www.wunderground.com/history/daily/de/munich/EDDM.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the gear icon next to the search bar and switch the Temperature setting between °F and °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Forecasts from agencies including the UK Met Office center Munich’s August 19 maximum near 28–30 °C under mostly sunny skies, light westerly flow, and modest daytime heating that favors peak readings in this narrow band. Trader consensus, reflected in the 44 % probability on 29 °C and 36 % on 30 °C, aligns with model guidance showing limited cloud cover and no strong frontal systems to suppress insolation or enhance mixing. Historical August climatology for southern Bavaria supports occasional 29–30 °C days when high pressure dominates, while the low odds on extremes above 31 °C or below 27 °C reflect the narrow uncertainty range typical one day ahead of resolution. Updated model runs tomorrow morning will refine the final observed high before markets settle.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent Met Office guidance and ensemble model consensus point to a highest temperature of 22–23°C in London on August 20, as an unsettled Atlantic flow brings patchy rain and increased cloud cover that limits daytime heating. With the date only two days ahead, short-range forecasts show modest afternoon maxima near or slightly above the long-term August average of roughly 21–22°C, with showers and variable winds preventing stronger warming. Traders assign the highest implied probabilities to these outcomes because model runs continue to favor limited insolation and modest thermal advection rather than clear, anticyclonic conditions that could push readings toward 24–25°C. Minor shifts in the timing or intensity of rain bands remain the main source of uncertainty ahead of the next forecast updates.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent Japan Meteorological Agency guidance and ensemble model consensus indicate a mostly cloudy day with scattered showers for Tokyo on August 20, supporting maximum temperatures near 32–33°C and limiting surface heating. Mid-August climatology shows a long-term average high of about 31°C, but elevated humidity and reduced solar insolation from cloud cover are capping extremes below 34°C while steering patterns and residual monsoon moisture suppress cooler outcomes. Short-term model runs exhibit limited spread, with urban heat-island effects and boundary-layer conditions reinforcing the current trader weighting toward 31–32°C as the most probable resolution range ahead of peak afternoon heating.

This range reflects typical late-summer high-pressure patterns that suppress cloud cover and allow modest warming above the long-term August average high near 22–23°C, without the stronger advection or subsidence needed for 30°C or higher. Recent model runs show limited spread, supporting the combined 79% trader consensus on 28–29°C while assigning only modest odds to 30°C. Updated guidance closer to the daily peak will refine these values, as small shifts in cloud timing or boundary-layer mixing can alter the observed high by 1–2°C.

eventMetadata.context_description: National Weather Service forecasts and ensemble guidance for August 19, 2026, position the highest temperature in New York City most likely in the mid to upper 80s, with point forecasts centering near 84–87°F under a building surface high, southerly flow, and partly to mostly sunny skies. This setup supports modest warming above the Central Park August average of 83°F amid an overall warmer-than-average monthly pattern. Market-implied odds concentrate on the 86–87°F bin at 64.5% because models show limited risk of strong convection or sea-breeze cooling that could cap readings in the mid-80s, while afternoon cloud cover and humidity keep the chance of reaching the low 90s below 25%. Updated guidance continues to reinforce this range ahead of final observations.

eventMetadata.context_description: **National Weather Service guidance for New York City on August 20 points to a mostly sunny morning with a high near 81°F before clouds increase and a 40-50% chance of showers develops in the afternoon.** This timing of potential convection, combined with light northwest winds and dewpoints in the upper 60s, favors a peak in the low 80s rather than pushing into the mid-80s. August climatology places the normal Central Park high near 83°F, but the current pattern—marked by a weaker Bermuda High and higher-than-average monthly temperatures overall—supports the market's tight clustering around the 80-83°F bins as traders weigh official forecasts against ensemble uncertainty and the narrow window for additional warming before any precipitation arrives.

These values align with late-August climatology for the region (historical averages ~23 °C) while reflecting current synoptic conditions that lack strong high-pressure subsidence or warm advection needed for extremes above 31 °C.

The market’s heavy weighting on 29 °C (56.5 % implied probability) followed by 30 °C (21.5 %) and 28 °C (15.5 %) reflects tight clustering in ensemble guidance and recent model runs showing only modest day-to-day variability. With resolution depending on the official maximum recorded at a standard station (typically Munich Airport or city observations), traders are emphasizing the narrow forecast range and low likelihood of significant model shifts on the final day. No major data releases or rapid changes in atmospheric patterns have altered this consensus in the past 24–48 hours.

eventMetadata.context_description: Current JMA guidance for August 21 shows mostly cloudy skies with afternoon thunderstorm chances, pointing to a daytime maximum near the 30.9 °C seasonal normal and supporting the tight clustering of market-implied odds around 30–32 °C. Subtropical high pressure maintains southerly flow and high humidity, yet increased moisture favors diurnal convection that reduces insolation and caps peak heating. Small shifts in the timing of cloud cover or shower onset—common model divergences two days out—can easily swing the observed maximum by 1–2 °C, which is why the leading outcomes remain closely matched. Urban heat-island effects in central Tokyo provide a modest boost above rural baselines, but any earlier or more widespread precipitation would favor the 30 °C or lower bins. Updated JMA and ensemble model runs expected over the next 24–48 hours will be the key catalyst for further movement.

Morning showers noted in some runs may modestly cap peak readings, while any late-day clearing or model revisions could nudge the outcome toward the upper end of the narrow distribution. Real-time observations and the final 24-hour maximum will resolve the market once the day closes.

This market will resolve based on the highest temperature recorded in the 'Daily Observations' table on Weather Underground, not the figure displayed in the 'Day High & Low' summary section; in the event of any discrepancy between the two, the Daily Observations table shall be the primary resolution source not the Day High & Low section.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded at the Munich Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 19 Aug '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from Wunderground, specifically the highest temperature recorded for all times on this day for the Munich Airport Station, available here: https://www.wunderground.com/history/daily/de/munich/EDDM.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the gear icon next to the search bar and switch the Temperature setting between °F and °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Forecasts from agencies including the UK Met Office center Munich’s August 19 maximum near 28–30°C under mostly sunny skies, light westerly flow, and modest daytime heating that favors peak readings in this narrow band. Trader consensus, reflected in the 63% implied probability on 29°C and 28% on 30°C, aligns with model guidance showing limited cloud cover and no strong frontal systems to suppress insolation or enhance mixing. Historical August climatology for southern Bavaria supports occasional 29–30°C days when high pressure dominates, while the low odds on extremes above 31°C or below 27°C reflect the narrow uncertainty range typical one day ahead of resolution. Updated model runs and official observations will refine the final measured high before markets settle.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent ensemble forecasts from the European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts and German Weather Service place Munich’s maximum temperature on August 20 in the 25–27°C range, driving the closely matched market probabilities for those outcomes. Variable high pressure combined with moderate southerly flow supports modest warming above the late-August climatological average of 22–24°C, while limited model spread on the timing of weak fronts or increased cloud cover creates the narrow uncertainty band. These factors explain why 28°C and higher remain low-probability outcomes without stronger warm advection, and why sub-24°C results would require greater-than-expected cooling from diurnal cloud development or frontal passage. Updated model runs and official observations tomorrow morning will provide the final resolution data.

eventMetadata.context_description: Trader consensus favors an 86-87°F high in New York City on August 19, reflecting National Weather Service and ensemble model consensus for mid-to-upper 80s under a building surface high with southerly flow and partly to mostly sunny skies. This aligns with the month’s warmer-than-average pattern, where Central Park highs have recently exceeded the 83°F climatological baseline. Afternoon cloud cover, shower timing, and sea-breeze effects introduce spread toward 88-89°F in some guidance, while limiting upside beyond that range. Latest observational trends and short-range model runs continue to anchor probabilities near the upper end of typical August variability without indicating significant deviations.
